chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, and he is unable to walk due to fear of the beast. If he stands to pray, he fears the beast during his bowing and prostration, and the beast is in front of him facing away from the Qiblah. If he turns towards the Qiblah, he fears the lion will leap upon him. How should he act? He said: He should face the lion, pray, and gesture with his head while standing, even if the lion is facing away from the Qiblah.
ai.seo_question: How should one pray if a wild animal is in front of them and they fear for their safety?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific jurisprudence of Salat al-Khawf (Prayer of Fear), illustrating the principle of prioritizing survival when facing imminent danger from a wild beast. It establishes that if facing the Qiblah endangers the worshipper, they may face the threat directly and perform standing prayer with head gestures (i'ma') rather than full bowing and prostration, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility in ritual form based on practical necessity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al-Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who faces the predatory wild animal and the time for the Salāt comes up, and he is not able upon the walking, fearing the predatory wild animal. So if he were to stand to Pray Salāt, he would fear the lion in his Rukū and his Sajdah, and the lion is in front of him upon (a direction) other than the Qiblah. So if he were to divert towards the Qiblah, he fears that the lion would leap upon him. How should he deal with it?’ So heasws said: ‘He should face the lion, and he should pray Salāt gesturing by his head with gestures, and he would be standing; and even if the lion was upon (a direction) other than the Qiblah’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far who has said the following:

“I once asked my brother, abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one who faces a beast and it is time for Salah (prayer). He is not able to walk, because of fear from the beast. If he stands up he fears to perform Ruku’ (bowing down on one’s knees) or Sujud (prostrations) with the beast in front of him in a direction other than that of al-Qiblah (al-Ka’bah). If he turns to al-Qiblah (al-Ka’bah), he fears the lion’s attack. What is he required to do in such case? He (the Imam) said, ‘ He faces the lion and performs his Salah (prayer) with gestures in a standing position, if the lion is in a direction other than that for al-Qiblah (al-Ka’bah).’”
